facts.fact: Image.save() of a float image made with images.new(float_buffer=True), file_format OPEN_EXR, wrote sRGB-encoded values into the EXR (0.5 -> 0.735, 2.0 -> 1.353, 0.18 -> 0.461), and the image's colour space read Linear Rec.709 before the save and sRGB after it; image.save_render(path) with the scene's format set to OPEN_EXR wrote the values unchanged

Bump's Distance is the height in scene units that one unit of the Height input stands for: on a ramp h = u (0..1 over 2 m, so 0.5 per metre), the normal matched normalize(-Distance x 0.5, 0, 1); the default Distance 0.001 tilts it by under 0.03 degrees, so a 0..1 texture at the default barely shows

Bump's Strength blends the bumped normal with the unbumped one and normalises (not a scale on the height): Strength 0.5 at Distance 1 gave the tilt of the normalised average, not of Distance 0.5; invert flips the slope's sign

A tangent-space Normal Map whose colour encodes the bumped normal (rgb = n x 0.5 + 0.5) gives the same normal as the Bump node, from a float EXR or an 8-bit PNG under Non-Color; the same PNG left in sRGB gives a different, wrong normal
Tangent space follows the UV map: red above 0.5 tilts the normal toward +U (here +x), green above 0.5 toward +V (here +y), the OpenGL convention; a DirectX-style map needs its green channel inverted
Normal Map's Strength changes the tilt away from the surface normal: for a map tilted 26.57 degrees, Strength 0.5 gave 13.29 degrees (the same as Bump's blend) and 2.0 gave 45.0 degrees

Object scale and the two nodes: at uniform scale 2 the same UV ramp spans 4 m and the bump's tilt fell to that of half the slope (Distance is in world units, not scaled with the object), while the normal map's normal did not change; at non-uniform scale (2, 2, 1) both flattened, because the normal map's tangents are transformed with the object

A tangent-space Normal Map on a quad with no UV map rendered without an error and gave the encoded normal, with the tangent along the object's local +x: rotating the object 90 degrees about z turned the tilt from world -x to world -y, as it did for the UV-mapped plane; Bump needs no UVs at all (here Object coordinates: h = x, 1 per metre)

Under a sun from -x at 45 degrees, a white diffuse surface with the bump and with the matching normal map rendered the same brightness, brighter than the flat surface as Lambert predicts; Cycles' Normal pass holds the bumped (shading) normal, not the geometric one
